51: 
52: A one-year issue of 7/8 percent certificates of indebtedness outstanding in the amount of $3,174 million matured on January 1, 1948. On December 19, 1947, the Secretary of the Treasury announced the offering of a new 12-month 1-1/8 percent certificate of indebtedness in exchange, par for par, for the maturing certificates. Cash subscriptions were not received. The new certificates are dated January 1, 1948, and bear interest from that date at the rate of 1-1/8 percent per annum. Interest will be paid in full with the principal on the maturity date, January 1, 1949. The certificates were issued in bearer form only, in denominations of $1,000, $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.
53: 
54: Reports to the Treasury on the ownership of Government securities indicate that on November 30, 1947, about 66 percent of the $3,134 million of certificates maturing January 1, 1948, were owned by commercial banks and Federal Reserve Banks. The ownership figures for November 30 are the latest which are available for holdings of both commercial banks and Federal Reserve Banks.
55: 
56: Subscription books were opened on December 19, and were closed at the close of business on December 27. Four hundred million dollars of the Federal Reserve Bank holdings of the maturing certificates of indebtedness were redeemed for cash. Exchange subscriptions for the new issue amounted to $2,592 million, leaving $142 million to be paid in cash to holders other than Federal Reserve Banks.

59: 
60: Additional reductions in Treasury bills outstanding were made in the first two weeks of December. The four issues maturing weekly during the month totaled $5.0 billion and the total refunded was $4.8 billion. Each of the first two maturing issues was reduced by $100 million.

65: 
66: Announcement was made by the Treasury Department on December 31, 1947, that in furtherance of the campaign to increase the sale of savings bonds, individual holders of Series C-1938 savings bonds, which started to mature January 1, 1948, would be permitted to reinvest the proceeds, as they mature, in Series E savings bonds currently on sale, without regard to the $5,000 (maturity value) annual limitation on E bond holdings. Since Series E bonds may be purchased only in the names of individuals, only those Series C-1938 savings bonds held by individuals are eligible for this privilege.
67: 
68: Any issuing agent qualified to cash savings bonds can accomplish this exchange by redeeming matured bonds and applying the proceeds to the purchase of new Series E bonds. Holders are permitted to reinvest any part of the proceeds of their maturing bonds to the extent of such denominational amount as the proceeds fully cover. The bonds may be exchanged also, of course, at any Federal Reserve Bank or branch, or at the Treasury Department.
